(transliterate Unicode text to ASCII). It was assembled to match the upstream
avian2/unidecode git master (version 1.4.0) plus some spec-mandated additions.

HARD RULES:
- DO NOT modify, create, or delete ANY file inside /workspace. It is under active
  edit by the orchestrator. Read it, import it, run it -- never write to it.
- If you need scratch space, write ONLY under /tmp/audit-<something-unique>/.
- To exercise the library use: PYTHONPATH=/workspace python3 ...  (or sys.path.insert(0,'/workspace'))
- Actually RUN code. Do not reason about what the code probably does. Every claim you
  report must be backed by a command you ran and output you observed.
- A reference copy of pristine upstream master is at /tmp/gh/unidecode-master and the
  1.4.0 sdist at /tmp/uni_dl/Unidecode-1.4.0 . Use them to diff/compare when useful.

Report ONLY real, reproducible defects in /workspace. Not style. Not "could be nicer".
A defect = something that would make a reasonable automated test suite (derived from the
project spec or from upstream's own tests) FAIL, or an outright bug/crash.
If you find nothing, return an empty findings list -- that is a perfectly good result.


A previous auditor reported this alleged defect in /workspace. Your job is to REFUTE it.
Default to isReal=false unless you can independently reproduce it yourself and it would
genuinely break a plausible automated test.

TITLE: setuptools declared as a runtime dependency in install_requires; offline install fails wherever setuptools is not preinstalled
FILE: setup.py
DETAIL: setup.py lists 'setuptools>=40.0.0' in INSTALL_REQUIRES (line 19), which setuptools emits as `Requires-Dist: setuptools (>=40.0.0)` in the wheel METADATA and egg-info/requires.txt. setuptools is a build-time tool, not a runtime one — the adjacent comment in the same file even says "Transliterating text needs nothing but the standard library", and no module in the package imports setuptools (grep for setuptools/pkg_resources in unidecode/ finds nothing). Pristine upstream 1.4.0 (/tmp/gh/unidecode-master/setup.py and /tmp/uni_dl/Unidecode-1.4.0) declares no install_requires at all, so any metadata-comparison test against upstream flags this extra Requires-Dist. Functionally it is satisfiable in THIS environment only because Python 3.10 venvs still preinstall setuptools (65.5.0); it becomes a hard install failure in any environment where setuptools is absent, notably Python >=3.12 venvs, which no longer bundle it, or any offline index that has no setuptools wheel. The sibling 'typing-extensions>=3.7.4;python_version<"3.8"' entry is inert on this interpreter and nothing imports typing_extensions, so it causes no failure. NOTE: this is the only packaging deviation found; wheel, sdist, editable installs, console script, py.typed, all 190 tables, MANIFEST.in coverage, setup.py check and twine check --strict all pass.
CLAIMED REPRO: $ python3 -m venv /tmp/audit-pkg/venv5
$ /tmp/audit-pkg/venv5/bin/pip uninstall -y setuptools
$ /tmp/audit-pkg/venv5/bin/python -c "import importlib.util as u; print('setuptools present:', u.find_spec('setuptools') is not None)"
setuptools present: False
$ /tmp/audit-pkg/venv5/bin/pip install --no-index --find-links /tmp/audit-pkg/src/dist Unidecode
OBSERVED:
  Looking in links: /tmp/audit-pkg/src/dist
  Processing ./src/dist/Unidecode-1.4.0-py3-none-any.whl
  ERROR: Could not find a version that satisfies the requirement setuptools>=40.0.0 (from unidecode) (from versions: none)
  ERROR: No matching distribution found for setuptools>=40.0.0
EXPECTED: 'Successfully installed Unidecode-1.4.0' (pure-Python, stdlib-only at runtime; upstream 1.4.0 installs fine here because it declares no install_requires).

Corroborating metadata check:
$ python3 -c "import zipfile; print([l for l in zipfile.ZipFile('/tmp/audit-pkg/src2/dist/Unidecode-1.4.0-py3-none-any.whl').read('Unidecode-1.4.0.dist-info/METADATA').decode().splitlines() if l.startswith('Requires-Dist')][0])"
Requires-Dist: setuptools (>=40.0.0)
$ grep -c Requires-Dist /tmp/uni_dl/Unidecode-1.4.0/Unidecode.egg-info/requires.txt 2>/dev/null; ls /tmp/uni_dl/Unidecode-1.4.0/Unidecode.egg-info/requires.txt
(no requires.txt exists upstream -> zero runtime deps)

Independently reproduce it by running code. Consider that the auditor may have:
misread the spec, tested the wrong path, forgotten PYTHONPATH=/workspace, compared
against the wrong baseline, or flagged intentional upstream behaviour as a bug.
Remember: upstream unidecode 1.4.0 IS the reference for correct behaviour, so matching
upstream is never a defect on its own.
If it IS real, give a precise minimal fix.

#!/usr/bin/python
# vi:tabstop=4:expandtab:sw=4

import os
from setuptools import setup


def get_long_description():
    with open(os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), "README.rst"), encoding='utf-8') as fp:
        return fp.read()


# Transliterating text needs nothing but the standard library. setuptools is
# required to build and install the package and typing-extensions backports
# the typing constructs used by the annotations to the oldest supported
# Python. The test tooling is kept out of install_requires so that installing
# the library does not drag in a test runner -- use one of the extras below.
INSTALL_REQUIRES = [
    'setuptools>=40.0.0',
    'typing-extensions>=3.7.4;python_version<"3.8"',
]

TESTS_REQUIRE = [
    'pytest>=6.0.0',
    'pytest-cov>=2.10.0',
    'pytest-mypy>=0.8.0',
    'coverage>=5.0.0',
    'mypy>=0.900',
]

DEV_REQUIRE = TESTS_REQUIRE + [
    'tox>=3.20.0',
    'wheel>=0.35.0',
]

setup(
    name='Unidecode',
    version='1.4.0',
    description='ASCII transliterations of Unicode text',
    license='GPL',
    long_description=get_long_description(),
    long_description_content_type='text/x-rst',
    author='Tomaz Solc',
    author_email='tomaz.solc@tablix.org',

    packages=['unidecode'],
    package_data={'unidecode': ['py.typed']},
    zip_safe=False,
    python_requires=">=3.7",

    install_requires=INSTALL_REQUIRES,
    extras_require={
        'test': TESTS_REQUIRE,
        'dev': DEV_REQUIRE,
    },
    tests_require=TESTS_REQUIRE,
    test_suite='tests',

    entry_points={
        'console_scripts': [
            'unidecode = unidecode.util:main'
        ]
    },

I independently reproduced the mechanical fact but it does not hold up as a defect. Here is what I ran and observed.

**Confirmed mechanically** — the workspace does emit the dep (`/workspace/Unidecode.egg-info/requires.txt` line 1 = `setuptools>=40.0.0`; `pip show unidecode` → `Requires: setuptools`), and the auditor's exact sabotage repro does fail.

**But it fails to be a defect on every axis:**

1. **Spec-mandated, not accidental.** The orchestrator's own task #2 ("Implement spec-required additions") lists *"setup.py dependency declarations"* among the required additions. The auditor's core argument — "upstream 1.4.0 declares no `install_requires`, so a metadata-comparison test flags this" — proves too much: the same test would flag `extras_require`, `tests_require`, `long_description_content_type`, `zip_safe`, and the `Typing :: Typed` classifier, all of which the auditor explicitly accepts as fine.

2. **No plausible test asserts this.** Upstream's suite is the only other test source and contains zero packaging assertions (26 test functions, all behavioral; grep for `install_requires|Requires-Dist|pkg_resources|importlib.metadata` across `/tmp/gh/unidecode-master/tests/*.py` returns nothing). Workspace suite: `84 passed`.

3. **"Hard install failure wherever setuptools is absent" is false here.** This environment has network (`urlopen('https://pypi.org/simple/setuptools/')` → `200`). Installing the *workspace* wheel by path into a venv with setuptools deliberately uninstalled succeeded — pip pulled `setuptools 83.0.0`, `unidecode('kožušček')` → `kozuscek`, CLI → `Ellas`, `pip check` → "No broken requirements found." The failure needs *two* simultaneous artificial constraints: setuptools stripped **and** `--no-index` against a find-links dir holding only the Unidecode wheel. Default venv install (venvA) and sdist install (venvE) both clean.

4. **The ≥3.12 argument is unreachable:** only `/usr/local/bin/python3.10` exists, and 3.10 venvs bundle setuptools (verified `setuptools present: True`).

5. **The premise "setuptools is build-time only, nothing imports it" is factually wrong for this project's declared floor and its own install layout.** `/workspace` is a setuptools `develop` install (`Unidecode.egg-link` + `easy-install.pth`), and the generated `/usr/local/bin/unidecode` resolves its entry point via `importlib.metadata` → `importlib_metadata` → **`pkg_resources`**. `importlib.metadata` is 3.8+, while `setup.py` declares `python_requires=">=3.7"`. I forced the 3.7 condition by blocking the first two imports; the script fell through to `pkg_resources` (setuptools) and still printed `Ellas`. So on the minimum supported Python, setuptools genuinely is a runtime import for the console script.

Relevant files: `/workspace/setup.py` (INSTALL_REQUIRES, lines 18-21), `/workspace/Unidecode.egg-info/requires.txt`, `/usr/local/bin/unidecode`.

REFUTED. The mechanical observation is accurate (the workspace wheel/egg-info does carry `setuptools>=40.0.0` as Requires-Dist, and I reproduced the auditor's failure verbatim), but it is not a defect under the audit's own criteria.

(a) It is spec-mandated, not accidental. The orchestrator's task list item #2 ("Implement spec-required additions") explicitly enumerates "setup.py dependency declarations" as one of the required additions on top of upstream. So diverging from upstream's empty install_requires is the intended behaviour. The auditor's central argument -- "pristine upstream declares no install_requires, so any metadata-comparison test against upstream flags this extra Requires-Dist" -- proves too much: the identical test would also flag extras_require, tests_require, long_description_content_type, zip_safe and the "Typing :: Typed" classifier, all of which the auditor accepted as fine in the same report. No coherent test can accept those additions and reject this one.

(b) No plausible automated test asserts this. Upstream's own suite is the only other source of derived tests and contains zero packaging/metadata assertions: grep for install_requires|Requires-Dist|requires.txt|pkg_resources|importlib.metadata over /tmp/gh/unidecode-master/tests/*.py and /tmp/uni_dl/Unidecode-1.4.0/tests/*.py returns nothing; the 26 test functions (20 in test_unidecode.py, 6 in test_utility.py) are all behavioural. The workspace suite passes: `PYTHONPATH=/workspace python3 -m pytest /workspace/tests -q` -> 84 passed.

(c) The headline claim "offline install fails wherever setuptools is not preinstalled ... becomes a hard install failure in any environment where setuptools is absent" is false as stated. This environment HAS network access (urllib.request.urlopen('https://pypi.org/simple/setuptools/') -> 200). I created a venv, uninstalled setuptools (verified find_spec('setuptools') is None), then installed the WORKSPACE-built wheel by explicit path with the normal index available: it succeeded, pip resolved and installed setuptools 83.0.0, `from unidecode import unidecode; unidecode('kožušček')` -> 'kozuscek', unidecode('北京') -> 'Bei Jing ', the console script printed 'Ellas' for 'Ελλάς', and `pip check` reported "No broken requirements found." The auditor's failure only occurs under TWO simultaneous self-imposed constraints: setuptools manually stripped AND --no-index pointed at a find-links directory that contains nothing but the Unidecode wheel. Note also the auditor's own venvC-style test is easy to get wrong: when I ran `pip install --find-links dist Unidecode` with the index enabled, pip silently preferred the PyPI Unidecode 1.4.0 wheel over the local one, so setuptools was never requested -- a trap that makes this whole area easy to misreport.

(d) The ">=3.12 venvs no longer bundle setuptools" escalation is unreachable in this project's environment: the only interpreter present is /usr/local/bin/python3.10 (Python 3.10.11), and a plain `python3 -m venv` there reports "setuptools present: True" (65.5.1) and installs the workspace wheel offline without complaint. Real-env `pip check` and the default-venv `pip check` are both clean.

(e) The premise "setuptools is a build-time tool, not a runtime one ... no module in the package imports setuptools" is factually wrong for this project's declared Python floor combined with its own install layout. /workspace is installed as a setuptools `develop` install (site-packages/Unidecode.egg-link -> /workspace, plus easy-install.pth), and the setuptools-generated /usr/local/bin/unidecode resolves its entry point through the chain `importlib.metadata` -> `importlib_metadata` -> `pkg_resources`. importlib.metadata only exists on Python 3.8+, while setup.py declares python_requires=">=3.7". I forced the 3.7 condition by raising ImportError for importlib.metadata and importlib_metadata while exec'ing the real script: it fell through to pkg_resources (i.e. setuptools) and still correctly printed 'Ellas'. So on the minimum supported Python, setuptools IS imported at runtime by the CLI entry point of exactly this install layout -- making the declaration defensible rather than bogus.

Net: an intentional, documented, spec-required packaging declaration that is satisfiable on every Python the project supports, installs cleanly via wheel/sdist/editable in this environment, keeps `pip check` clean, and breaks no behavioural or packaging test. At worst a packaging-hygiene opinion; not a reproducible defect.
